text.p: Intel Corp said Monday it unveiled its new 233-megahertz (MHz) Pentium processor for mainstream consumer personal computers that run applications designed for Intel's MMX technology.
In 1,000-unit quantities, the company said the 233-MHz chip in ceramic or plastic pin grid array (PPGA) packages is priced at $594 and is immediately available.
The company and that some PC manufacturers are expected to introduce systems today, some bundled with a variety of software designed using Intel's MMX technology.
MMX technology allows for features such as life-like color, video and graphics, real-time animation and three-dimensional audio and lighting.
In an earlier statement, Intel said the 233-MHz chip, the fastest in its Pentium line, will appear this fall in personal computers priced at $2,000 to $2,500.
